node.label: John M. MacKenzie
node.date_label: Propaganda and Empire (1984) · Imperialism and Popular Culture: edited collection (1986) · The Empire of Nature (1988)
node.description: A historian of empire who made its cultural presence in Britain, and its environmental history overseas, central subjects of imperial history. As founding editor of Manchester University Press’s Studies in Imperialism series he set out to examine how imperialism shaped the dominant societies as well as those they ruled; Propaganda and Empire (1984) studied the manipulation of British public opinion. The Empire of Nature (1988) connected hunting and conservation with British rule in Africa and India. Orientalism: History, Theory and the Arts (1995) challenged Edward Said’s generalizations through empirical study of the arts, as Berny Sèbe describes; Said in turn criticized an approach he associated with MacKenzie that treated culture as propaganda. His exchanges with Bernard Porter, after Porter’s The Absent-Minded Imperialists (2004), became among the most-read items in the Journal of Imperial and Commonwealth History.
